subject: RE: FOI / Records Request – Deaths of William (Billy) Buckler (1990) and Mary Doreen Williams (1983)
source: Original email in the family's Gmail (read-only export); contact details redacted.
text:
Good morning, Requester
Thank you for your prompt reply.
I have checked our system for any records relating to the two cases you have asked information for.
Unfortunately, I am unable to locate any details on the Late Mr William Buckler or the late Mary Doreen Williams.
Cardiff and Vale cases prior to 2002 should be with the Glamorgan Archivist, you can contact them on Tel; [phone redacted] or [email redacted] 
I hope this information helps and I wish you the best in your search.
Kind Regards
Bev

From: Requester  
Sent: 21 August 2026 08:47
To: Coroner Admin  
Subject: Re: FOI / Records Request – Deaths of William (Billy) Buckler (1990) and Mary Doreen Williams (1983)


Bev,

Thank you for clarifying the position regarding the Freedom of Information Act.

I understand that coroners and their records are not subject to the FOI access regime. I am therefore not seeking to pursue the matter as an FOI request if that is not the appropriate route.

My primary purpose is to establish whether either of these deaths was ever referred to the coroner and, if so, whether any surviving record exists and what lawful route is available for an interested family member to obtain information from it.

I would therefore be grateful if you could clarify the following, insofar as you are able:

  1.  Whether your office has any record or index indicating that either William (Billy) Buckler, who died at Llandough Hospital on or about 29 May 1990, or Mary Doreen Williams, whose death was registered in March 1983 in South Glamorgan (Vol. 28, p. 3029), was reported to or dealt with by the coroner;
  2.  If either death was the subject of a coroner's investigation, whether an inquest, post-mortem examination or other coroner's investigation took place;
  3.  Whether any historical record relating to either death remains in the custody of the coroner's service, or whether such records have been transferred to another archive, authority or successor body;
  4.  If records exist but cannot be disclosed directly, what procedure is available for a descendant or other interested person to establish the basic factual information concerning the case;
  5.  If your office has no record whatsoever of either death, whether that means that no coroner's record exists, or simply that the surviving records are no longer held by your office.

I am particularly interested in establishing the documentary chain rather than necessarily seeking disclosure of confidential medical information. A confirmation that a death was, or was not, referred to the coroner would itself be useful.

If you are not the appropriate office to answer these historical-record questions, I would be grateful if you could identify the relevant archive, successor body or other custodian to whom I should direct the enquiry.

Thank you again for your assistance.

Regards,



Requester 



On Fri, 21 Aug 2026, 04:33 Coroner Admin,  > wrote:
Good morning, Requester
Thank you for your e-mail dated 20/08/2026.

Although appointed and paid for by local councils, the coroner is not a local government officer but holds office under the Crown.

Coroners are not designated as public authorities under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and therefore their records are not subject to the information access regime of this Act.

Please let me know if I can be of further assistance.
Kind Regards
Bev Morgan


From: Requester  >
Sent: 20 August 2026 20:34
To: Coroner Admin  >
Subject: FOI / Records Request – Deaths of William (Billy) Buckler (1990) and Mary Doreen Williams (1983)

Dear Coroner’s Office,

I am writing under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and as an interested person to request any records held by the South Wales Central Coroner’s Service relating to the following two deaths:

1. William (Billy) Buckler
   - Late of Great House Farm, Llandough
   - Died at Llandough Hospital on or about 29 May 1990, aged 41
   - Reported cause: heart attack
   - Funeral 5 June 1990, Bethesda Chapel, Dinas Powys; interment St Michael’s Church, Michaelston-le-Pit

2. Mary Doreen Williams
   - Born 10 August 1913
   - Death registered March 1983, South Glamorgan (Vol 28, Page 3029)

Please advise whether either death was reported to the Coroner, whether a post-mortem or inquest was held, and what documentation (reports, police referrals, hospital communications, etc.) remains available. Please also confirm the procedure, identification required, any fees, and timescales for release to next-of-kin or interested persons.

I can supply further identifying details, proof of interest, and contemporary newspaper cuttings / family notes upon request.

Thank you for your assistance.

Yours faithfully,

Requester
